jobs.description:
Lead our NP/PA Residents!

The Residency Program Director will lead the NP/PA Residency Program, leading and supervising
other faculty in precepting and teaching Nurse Practitioner and Physician Assistant Residents and leading the team responsible for resident selection and evaluation, curricular evaluation and development, and integration of the program into Petaluma Health Center’s mission and goals. The Program Director ideally would also serve as Team Director of the residency team, conditional on appropriate experience to assume that position. (Please refer to Associate Clinical Director Primary Care Job Description). As a clinician, they will provide quality primary medical care in a collaborative, compassionate, and caring environment. They will work as an integral part of the medical staff by participating in all strategic initiatives of Petaluma Health Center. Perform other duties as assigned, including but not limited to after -hours call,weekend clinics, and assignment to outside locations within PHC federal scope.

Grant-Funded/Limited-Duration Assignment:
This position is grant-funded and is intended to support the NP/PA Residency Program during the applicable grant cycle. Continued employment in this role is contingent upon available funding, continuation of the residency program, program needs, operational needs, and PHC’s discretion. The position may end, be extended, or be modified based on changes to funding, grant requirements, residency program needs, or PHC’s business needs. Residency:
Develop, implement, coordinate, integrate, and evaluate the work of the residency program to
assure attainment of program goals
Provide direct clinical teaching in both didactic and clinical settings
Lead team designing program guidelines, didactics, and residents’ schedules
Assist residents in achieving learning objectives in all desired areas of care and with a deep
understanding of PHC’s mission and culture
Supervise precepting, including providing training, evaluation, and feedback for preceptors
Assist in establishing and coordinating clinical rotations, both within PHC and with outside agencies
Coordinate regular evaluation of resident progress and performance, including for post -residency employment
Collaborate with operations and clinic administrators to ensure residents meet goals for number of patient visits completed during the twelve month program
Collaborate with operations and team manager to integrate residents into existing services and ensure that residents are part of the PHC clinic culture
Maintain program accreditation including any necessary reports or site visits
Create annual budget and work with health center staff to integrate budget within primary care
Support, apply for, and manage outside funding opportunities, including federal and state grants, and ensure timely completion of grant-related reporting, documentation, deliverables, and compliance requirements.
Manage relationship with collaborating academic institutions
Support grant-funded residency program operations, including implementation of grant-related

guidelines

Meet all time commitments by arriving on time to the clinic and working entire shift or more as

Assistant Residency

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Lead a statewide movement, shape what comes next, and help Women4Change turn bold ideas into meaningful action for women across Indiana.

About The Role

The Chief Executive Officer leads Women4Change Indiana, a nonpartisan, statewide nonprofit C3/C4 organization whose mission is to equip Hoosiers to engage in democracy to improve outcomes for women through community-building and advocacy.

This role works in close partnership with a Board of Directors and wears many hats – strategic, operational, financial, and programmatic – to advance the organization’s mission, ensuring alignment between long-term vision, programmatic impact, and organizational sustainability. This leader is comfortable rolling up their sleeves and leading a small, dedicated staff, fostering a culture grounded in equity and inclusion and reflecting the organization’s values.

As Women4Change's primary public representative, the CEO elevates organizational visibility across Indiana, engages stakeholders, strengthens partnerships, and positions the organization as a trusted voice on issues affecting women, their families, and their communities. With strong business judgment, the CEO aligns financial resources with strategic priorities, ensuring both mission impact and long-term viability. Working with the Board, staff, and key stakeholders, the CEO implements Women4Change's strategic priorities, evaluates outcomes, and adapts to evolving opportunities and challenges.

About You

Women4Change seeks a principled leader with a growth mindset and strong commitment to advancing opportunities and outcomes for women. The ideal candidate has a passion for advocacy, social justice, and women’s empowerment and can lead a small, dynamic organization, inspire diverse stakeholders, and translate vision into measurable results. This individual brings a collaborative leadership style, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate complex civic and policy environments with integrity, curiosity, and effectiveness.

The successful candidate is an experienced advocate with a track record of navigating state-level public policy, building organizational capacity, leading effective teams, and driving meaningful impact. They are a clear communicator, skilled relationship-builder, and credible public voice. This leader demonstrates resilience, adaptability, and the ability to unify diverse perspectives around shared goals.

What You'll Do

Strategic Leadership and Organizational Vision

In partnership with the Board of Directors, the CEO helps to define and advance a clear, compelling vision for Women4Change that reflects its mission and values. This leader develops and executes strategic plans, establishes measurable goals, and ensures accountability through regular evaluation and reporting. The CEO drives organizational growth by securing funding and increasing organizational visibility and engagement, while balancing mission impact with financial sustainability.

Resource Development and Financial Stewardship

The CEO executes comprehensive fundraising efforts, expanding and diversifying revenue across individual, corporate, and foundation sources. This includes cultivating major donors, strengthening existing relationships, and identifying new funding opportunities. The CEO ensures sound financial management, oversees budgeting processes, and aligns resources with strategic priorities to support long-term organizational health.

External Leadership and Partnerships

Serving as the primary spokesperson, the CEO represents Women4Change with credibility, vision, and clarity across public, private, and civic sectors. This leader builds and sustains strategic partnerships, engages policymakers and community leaders, and fosters coalitions that advance shared goals. The CEO strengthens the organization’s brand and visibility through effective communication, public engagement, and media presence.

Advocacy and Policy Leadership

Women4Change operates through a dual-entity structure that includes both a 501(c)(3) charitable organization and a 501(c)(4) action fund. This structure enables the organization to advance its mission through education, research, and community engagement, while also supporting advocacy and policy efforts that drive systemic change, inform, mobilize, and empower stakeholders, and maintain compliance with applicable nonprofit regulations. The CEO ensures that advocacy efforts are strategic, collaborative, and responsive to the needs of women across Indiana.

Board Relations and Governance

The CEO partners closely with the Board of Directors to support strong governance practices. This includes facilitating effective communication, providing strategic guidance, and ensuring the Board has the information and resources needed to fulfill its fiduciary responsibilities. The CEO supports Board development, engagement, and alignment with organizational priorities.

Organizational Leadership and Culture

The CEO recruits, develops, and retains a talented and diverse team, fostering a workplace culture rooted in respect, accountability, and inclusion. This leader sets clear expectations, supports professional growth, and ensures that staff are empowered to achieve organizational goals. The CEO promotes collaboration, innovation, and shared ownership of the mission.

What the Next CEO Will Be Asked to Build

Based on the transition process, the board has identified the following as the highest-priority areas for the incoming CEO to address in their first 18 months:

Operational Infrastructure - Complete the modernization of internal systems, documentation, and workflows to match the organization's external reputation
CRM & Data Management - Lead or oversee resolution of the EveryAction database challenges; manual workarounds are not sustainable. Consider forming a technology task force.
Fundraising Diversification - Move beyond reliance on a small number of donors and grants; build an annual giving program and cultivate a broader individual donor base
Governing Board Transition - Complete the shift from working board to governing board, with clearly defined roles, responsibilities, and committee structure between board, CEO, and staff
Statewide Expansion - Deepen reach beyond the Indianapolis metro through local ambassador models, listening sessions, and coalition partnerships
C3/C4 Clarity - Establish clear structures and resource allocation between the two entities, particularly as staff time is split across both

What You'll Bring

Leadership experience in nonprofit, public, or private sector organizations
Demonstrated success in strategic planning, organizational sustainability, and operational leadership
Proven fundraising experience, including major gifts and institutional funding
Strong financial acumen, including budgeting and resource allocation
Experience working with or supporting governing boards
Ability to build partnerships across community, business, and government sectors
Strong communication and public engagement skills
Understanding of policy, advocacy, and civic engagement landscapes
Commitment to equity, inclusion, and collaborative leadership
Experience in statewide or multi-regional organizations preferred

This position requires a high level of engagement, visibility, and commitment to advancing Women4Change's mission across Indiana. You are expected to work in downtown Indianapolis three days per week. This role also requires frequent evening and weekend presence at events statewide.

What We Offer

The salary range for this position will be commensurate with experience. We offer an annual benefits allowance to cover health insurance. Women4Change observes ten paid holidays each year and offers Paid Time Off and Sick Leave.

About Women4Change

Women4Change Indiana is a nonpartisan, statewide organization that equips and mobilizes Hoosiers to drive measurable improvements in women’s health, civic engagement, economic stability, and personal safety.

In a rapidly shifting civic, healthcare, and economic landscape, Women4Change has become a trusted statewide voice and civic infrastructure, reaching thousands of Hoosiers annually through an integrated strategy of communications, coalition-building, and advocacy that ensures women’s voices are present in public discourse and policymaking.

W4C integrates grassroots engagement, civic education, and policy advocacy through a dual 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) structure, translating informed communities into legislative impact and systems-level change across Indiana.

The next CEO will lead and scale this work across a continuum of impact by empowering, educating, collaborating, activating, and advocating to expand influence, strengthen civic participation, and advance equitable outcomes statewide. This leader will deepen strategic partnerships, expand our diversified funding model, and lead fund development by growing and stewarding a broad donor base and aligning resources to ensure the organization’s capacity, sustainability, and agility in critical moments shaping Indiana’s civic and policy landscape.
We are an equal opportunity employer.

How to Apply

Submit all applications through our HR Partner, Deep End Talent Strategies, via this career portal. Please do not contact the organization directly, as our small team focuses on mission-critical work. The application will ask you a few questions, including three professional references, which we will keep confidential and not contact until the final step in our process.

While we anticipate keeping it open until at least mid-October, we will review applications as soon as they are submitted and close this process when we are pleased with the pool of viable candidates.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Wipfli is assisting our client, Kewa Pueblo Health Corporation (KPHC), in seeking an experienced and mission-driven Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead the organization. This is a unique opportunity for an accomplished healthcare executive to guide a tribally chartered healthcare organization, strengthen programs and services, and help ensure the highest quality of care for the Santo Domingo Pueblo community.

Located between Albuquerque and Santa Fe on the Santo Domingo (Kewa) Pueblo, KPHC is a community-based health center operating under an Indian Health Service (IHS) Title I contract. Dedicated to ensuring health and wellness through excellence in healthcare with respect for culture, KPHC has grown from a primary care clinic into a comprehensive, multidisciplinary health system offering primary care, dental, optometry, pharmacy, behavioral health, public health, and specialty services, helping community members and patients access high-quality care close to home.

Reporting directly to the KPHC Board of Directors, the CEO is responsible for the overall administration and programmatic oversight of all KPHC programs and services, including the Santo Domingo Health Center. The CEO exercises executive authority for operational decisions, works closely with the Board on the management and direction of the Health Center, and provides leadership across operations, quality, compliance, finance, workforce development, strategic planning, and community relationships.

Key Responsibilities

Executive Leadership and Organizational Direction

Provide overall leadership and direction for KPHC programs, services, facilities, and health services provided to the community.
Work closely with the KPHC Board of Directors to manage and direct the Corporation’s programs and services.
Set and advance the mission, vision, and values of KPHC programs and services.
Lead long-range program planning and development of a strategic plan that addresses the health needs of the Santo Domingo Pueblo.
Make operational decisions, recommend new or revised policies, and ensure consistent implementation of approved policies and procedures.
Maintain ongoing, effective communication throughout the Corporation.

Operations, Quality, and Regulatory Compliance

Plan, organize, and direct facility operations to support quality care and the financial integrity of KPHC.
Coordinate quality assurance, quality improvement, and regulatory compliance across services offered to the community.
Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, Board policies, medical staff requirements, AAAHC standards, and other regulatory agencies.
Oversee systems for patient grievances, external appeals, adverse or sentinel event reporting, privacy, fraud and abuse prevention, and NPDB reporting.
Ensure appropriate maintenance and improvements for all KPHC facilities, grounds, and infrastructure.

Financial Stewardship and Resource Development

Collaborate with the Chief Financial Officer to monitor accounting, budgeting, responsibility reporting, internal controls, auditing, and cost reporting systems.
Oversee financial reporting, budget preparation and maintenance, billing, payroll, and related fiscal policies.
Prepare and administer the annual budget in coordination with the Finance Department and advise executive staff and the Board regarding shortages or needed adjustments.
Pursue alternate resources to support program activity, including grants, contracts, staffing agreements, and third-party reimbursements.

Encourage integration of the medical facility and services with the community through communication, visibility, and public outreach.

Experience with human resources management and the development and administration of financial management processes and systems required.
Knowledge of rural, community-oriented healthcare delivery systems and associated regulations and standards.
Knowledge and experience with Public Law 93-638 Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act contracting and the Indian Health Service system.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Grants Management
jobs.description:
The Skoll Foundation is hiring a Managing Director
of Grants Management
based in Washington, D.C. The Managing Director of Grants Management is eligible for a hybrid work schedule, including Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday required on-site in the Washington, D.C. office.

Skoll is a private grantmaking foundation that seeks to build a sustainable world of peace and prosperity for all by investing in, connecting, and championing social entrepreneurs and other social innovators. Together, we advance bold and equitable solutions to the world’s most pressing problems. The Skoll Foundation fosters a mission and values-based approach to the work we do focused on the vision of doing good.

Position Description

Reporting directly to the General Counsel, the Managing Director of Grants Management leads the Foundation’s grants management team in the execution and fulfillment of Foundation grants designed by our program teams. This role leads the short- and long-term strategy for grants management, including supporting the administration of approximately $100 million in grants each year. The Managing Director will be an internal expert on private foundation grantmaking, will provide support and training on grantmaking practices within the Foundation, and will build strong working relationships across programs to execute grantmaking strategies and advance the Foundation’s mission. The Managing Director serves as a trusted advisor and key partner to a wide range of internal and external stakeholders and directs a centralized approach to grantmaking systems, compliance, policies, and processes that are optimized for the Foundation’s innovative grantmaking environment. The Managing Director will also oversee external grants management vendor relationships and partners (Silicon Valley Community Foundation, Submittable, etc.) in the execution of the Foundation’s grantmaking activities and will consider ways to continually advance the efficiency and effectiveness of the Foundation’s grantmaking operations. The Managing Director will have one direct report, the Grants Manager. With a team of this size, both roles are expected to work directly on the grants pipeline: the Managing Director will regularly review and process grants alongside the Grants Manager, in addition to leading the function's strategy and standards. 

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

Strategy and Leadership

Provide leadership on the design and day-to-day operations of grants management, with a keen eye for efficiency and service quality. Build and maintain feedback mechanisms to ensure early detection of end-user problems. Apply foresight and judgment in adjusting grants management service, training, and communications to support program goals. 

Design and manage the overall grant workflow to support the full grant lifecycle, including pipeline management, grant recommendation, board approval process, grant agreement execution, payments, amendments, and reporting. Identify opportunities to streamline and improve the grantmaking workflow, further partner with external vendors, and enhance user training on systems and processes.

Partner with Finance on short- and long-term grants budget planning, including the development of the annual grant allocation and payout. Regularly advise teams on progress toward the current fiscal year’s grant payout while also ensuring flexibility in future years. 

Support the development of the Grants Manager, overseeing training, professional development, and performance management. 

Grants Management

Oversee all aspects of pre-and post-award grant activities, including supporting the full lifecycle of the grant process, from review, approval, payment, reporting, amendments, and closeout.

Review all grants, programmatic contracts, and Program-Related Investments for compliance with IRS regulations and Foundation requirements, working in partnership with the Grants Manager and collaborating with legal to ensure resolution of complex grantmaking issues, as needed.

Regularly participate in program meetings to advise and guide teams on appropriate charitable giving mechanisms to achieve programmatic objectives and impact, necessary legal due diligence, and to collaborate on pipeline planning.

Serve as primary relationship manager for the Foundation’s grantmaking partner, Silicon Valley Community Foundation, in the administration of the Skoll Fund, including coordinating fund grant recommendations, reconciling grants management system data against provider records, monitoring compliance with fund requirements, and partnering with Finance and Legal on entity selection for grant awards.

Develop institutional grantmaking policies and procedures for staff and grantees. This includes overseeing the development and maintenance of a grants management manual that joins the Foundation’s grantmaking policies, processes, and tools with complete grantmaking system documentation.

In close partnership with the Finance Department, oversee development of the annual grants-related data for Skoll Foundation’s 990-PF and Skoll Fund’s 990. Support Finance staff with the annual audit requirements.

Systems, Data, and Reporting

In partnership with the Technology Team, serve as the primary business owner and champion of the grants management functionality within the Foundation’s Salesforce system, with accountability for developing and prioritizing a roadmap of grantmaking enhancements and features. Partner with the Technology Team on infrastructure, security, integration standards, and architecture review.

Advise, coordinate, and collaborate on Foundation data strategy and governance for grantmaking data, including determining what data to capture and report for internal and external audiences.

In collaboration with internal teams, continually review, refine, and re-align on definitions and consistent uses of programmatic codes and tags, and regularly review grantmaking data to ensure accurate representation of information for data analysis purposes.

Prepare reports and data visualizations to provide a clear and compelling illustration of the Foundation’s grantmaking for internal and external stakeholders.

Design, monitor, and report on key operational metrics for the grantmaking function, e.g., annual trends on grant types and transaction volume, to support continuous improvement and inform resourcing decisions.

Continually stay abreast of new developments in Foundation grants management systems and technologies and their applicability to the evolving needs of the Foundation.  

Sector Engagement

Actively participate in philanthropy serving organizations, communities, and conferences as a Foundation representative.

Research, synthesize, and share knowledge on grantmaking practices and funding mechanisms that are relevant to the Foundation.

Advocate for equitable, values-aligned grantmaking approaches consistent with the Foundation’s mission.

Qualifications

A passion for the Foundation’s mission. 

Minimum of 10+ years of experience in grants management, nonprofit, and/or an operations environment with grantmaking responsibilities, including at least 5+ years in foundation grants management or grantmaking operations.

Robust knowledge of legal requirements and complexities of private foundation grantmaking is essential. This includes IRS expenditure responsibility requirements, equivalency determinations for international grants, fiscal sponsorship arrangements, and OFAC/sanctions screening protocols. Experience in a multi-entity grantmaking structure a plus.  Experience in a multi-entity grantmaking structure a plus.

A deep understanding of grantmaking processes and approaches and experience training staff on grantmaking policies and systems. 

Strong working knowledge of grants management systems, such as Salesforce, including experience prioritizing feature enhancements and partnering with other teams on configuration, testing, and rollout of new functionality. 

Experience designing and maintaining internal controls over private foundation grant disbursements, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting, and supporting both internal and external audit processes. 

Strong interpersonal and diplomacy skills and the ability to interact effectively with individuals at all levels of the organization.

Excellent organization, project management, problem-solving and workflow/process design skills.

Demonstrated ability to take initiative, manage heavy workload, and juggle competing priorities to meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment. 

Demonstrated ability to proactively communicate challenges and proposed solutions to problems. 

Demonstrated leadership and management skills, including organizational planning, goal setting, and people management and oversight. 

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

Able to work on-site three days a week including Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday in Washington, DC. 

Locational proximity of fifty miles or closer to the Washington, DC office required for consideration. 

Ability to travel up to 10% including domestic and international travel.

Must be legally authorized to work in the United States.

Other duties as assigned.

            Cultural Fit

Enthusiastic and flexible team player with humility, a positive demeanor, and exceptional service orientation; ready to roll up sleeves and collaborate across the Foundation’s small team.

A keen sense of integrity, professionalism, and commitment to creating a positive organizational culture.

Adaptable to change.

Desire to both create and execute. 

Interest in social innovation and alignment with the Skoll Foundation’s mission to catalyze transformational social change.

Proven ability to thrive in a collaborative, multi-cultural environment. 

Benefits 

The Skoll Foundation offers a comprehensive benefits package including a discretionary 10% employer sponsored retirement contribution, flexible time off, paid holidays, medical, dental, vision coverage, and generous retirement plan offerings. 

Salary Range

$181,642 to $290,628 

The full salary range for this role is $181,642 to $290,628 USD. New hires typically start between the range minimum and midpoint, or $181,642 to $236,187 USD, based on job-related skills, experience, and expertise evaluated during the interview process.

jobs.title: President & COO - Duke Health Cary
jobs.description:
At Duke Health, we're driven by a commitment to compassionate care that changes the lives of patients, their loved ones, and the greater community. No matter where your talents lie, join us and discover how we can advance health together.

The President & COO is the senior executive accountable for setting the vision and strategic direction for a new state-of-the-art community hospital campus. The first phase of the campus (98,000 SF medical office building) opened last year. In 2027, the 112,000 SF high end micro hospital including an ambulatory care center and first phase of the freestanding ED will open. In 2029, the third phase of the campus (430,000 SF) will open which will include expansion of the perioperative platform and ED services, a full-service cancer center and women’s health center along with 100 inpatient beds. The campus has capacity to grow to more than 500 inpatient beds. The remaining property on the campus will be used to develop a mix-use destination location including retail, walking trails, hotels, and other potential services.

Job Description

While overseeing the development of this key strategic project and establishing the culture, staffing and operational planning for phase 2 and 3 of the project is a critical component of this role. This role will evolve to be the executive in charge of this site after its opening with primary objectives being strategic development, construction oversight, activation, and ongoing clinical and administrative operations of the new full-service Duke Health Cary Hospital. This role converts enterprise strategy into a high-reliability operating model; ensures operational readiness and service excellence through Lean management principles; and delivers top outcomes in quality, safety, patient experience, access, throughput, workforce engagement, and financial performance.

The position will lead multi-year planning and execution for a major capital project (phase 3 and associated campus development), including scope, schedule, and budget governance, sustainability initiatives (electrification strategy, carbon reduction), and future-proofing for expansion (e.g., shell floors, parking, and infrastructure). The President & COO will oversee operational ramp-up, workforce planning, and community engagement to ensure successful go-live and long-term performance.

Additional Campus Facts

Building 100 (B100):

98,000 SF; fully open and dedicated to ambulatory care.

Building 200 (B200) Microhospital

112,000 SF; scheduled to open April 2027.

430,000 SF; scheduled to open Summer 2029 and will include a comprehensive cancer center (clinic space, infusion, LINAC), medical/surgical and ICU beds, labor & delivery, postpartum and NICU services, full perioperative and imaging platforms, emergency department, cath/EP/IR suites, and shelled space for future expansion.

84 acres.

Achieve best-in-class outcomes for safety, clinical quality, equity, and patient experience; drive reduction of serious safety events, infection prevention, pathway adherence, and environment-of-care standards.
Own hospital P&L; meet/exceed plan for margin, productivity, and cost performance; steward capital deployment and activation budgets.
Manage budget decisions and contingency strategies as outlined in board pre-read (e.g., electrification allowance, mechanical space adjustments, escalation allowances).
Lead campus master planning, facility programming and design, and construction contracting within Duke governance. Maintain disciplined scope, schedule, and budget controls; provide transparent progress reporting to DUHS leadership and boards.

Partner with DUHS Strategy/Finance and Development on funding and philanthropy for construction, technology, and programmatic priorities; implement robust financial controls and reporting.

Ensure continuous readiness for licensure, accreditation, and external regulatory reviews.
Sustain continuous regulatory readiness and exceptional patient experience outcomes.
Oversee equipment and technology selection/integration (EHR, digital front door, perioperative systems, imaging modalities, automated pharmacy/lab, care coordination tools) and patient-centered experience design including wayfinding, amenities, and service recovery.

Exempt

Lead a statewide movement, shape what comes next, and help Women4Change turn bold ideas into meaningful action for women across Indiana.

About The Role

The Chief Executive Officer leads Women4Change Indiana, a nonpartisan, statewide nonprofit C3/C4 organization whose mission is to equip Hoosiers to engage in democracy to improve outcomes for women through community-building and advocacy.

This role works in close partnership with a Board of Directors and wears many hats – strategic, operational, financial, and programmatic – to advance the organization’s mission, ensuring alignment between long-term vision, programmatic impact, and organizational sustainability. This leader is comfortable rolling up their sleeves and leading a small, dedicated staff, fostering a culture grounded in equity and inclusion and reflecting the organization’s values.

As Women4Change's primary public representative, the CEO elevates organizational visibility across Indiana, engages stakeholders, strengthens partnerships, and positions the organization as a trusted voice on issues affecting women, their families, and their communities. With strong business judgment, the CEO aligns financial resources with strategic priorities, ensuring both mission impact and long-term viability. Working with the Board, staff, and key stakeholders, the CEO implements Women4Change's strategic priorities, evaluates outcomes, and adapts to evolving opportunities and challenges.

About You

Women4Change seeks a principled leader with a growth mindset and strong commitment to advancing opportunities and outcomes for women. The ideal candidate has a passion for advocacy, social justice, and women’s empowerment and can lead a small, dynamic organization, inspire diverse stakeholders, and translate vision into measurable results. This individual brings a collaborative leadership style, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate complex civic and policy environments with integrity, curiosity, and effectiveness.

The successful candidate is an experienced advocate with a track record of navigating state-level public policy, building organizational capacity, leading effective teams, and driving meaningful impact. They are a clear communicator, skilled relationship-builder, and credible public voice. This leader demonstrates resilience, adaptability, and the ability to unify diverse perspectives around shared goals.

What You'll Do

Strategic Leadership and Organizational Vision

In partnership with the Board of Directors, the CEO helps to define and advance a clear, compelling vision for Women4Change that reflects its mission and values. This leader develops and executes strategic plans, establishes measurable goals, and ensures accountability through regular evaluation and reporting. The CEO drives organizational growth by securing funding and increasing organizational visibility and engagement, while balancing mission impact with financial sustainability.

Resource Development and Financial Stewardship

The CEO executes comprehensive fundraising efforts, expanding and diversifying revenue across individual, corporate, and foundation sources. This includes cultivating major donors, strengthening existing relationships, and identifying new funding opportunities. The CEO ensures sound financial management, oversees budgeting processes, and aligns resources with strategic priorities to support long-term organizational health.

External Leadership and Partnerships

Serving as the primary spokesperson, the CEO represents Women4Change with credibility, vision, and clarity across public, private, and civic sectors. This leader builds and sustains strategic partnerships, engages policymakers and community leaders, and fosters coalitions that advance shared goals. The CEO strengthens the organization’s brand and visibility through effective communication, public engagement, and media presence.

Advocacy and Policy Leadership

Women4Change operates through a dual-entity structure that includes both a 501(c)(3) charitable organization and a 501(c)(4) action fund. This structure enables the organization to advance its mission through education, research, and community engagement, while also supporting advocacy and policy efforts that drive systemic change, inform, mobilize, and empower stakeholders, and maintain compliance with applicable nonprofit regulations. The CEO ensures that advocacy efforts are strategic, collaborative, and responsive to the needs of women across Indiana.

Board Relations and Governance

The CEO partners closely with the Board of Directors to support strong governance practices. This includes facilitating effective communication, providing strategic guidance, and ensuring the Board has the information and resources needed to fulfill its fiduciary responsibilities. The CEO supports Board development, engagement, and alignment with organizational priorities.

Organizational Leadership and Culture

The CEO recruits, develops, and retains a talented and diverse team, fostering a workplace culture rooted in respect, accountability, and inclusion. This leader sets clear expectations, supports professional growth, and ensures that staff are empowered to achieve organizational goals. The CEO promotes collaboration, innovation, and shared ownership of the mission.

What the Next CEO Will Be Asked to Build

Based on the transition process, the board has identified the following as the highest-priority areas for the incoming CEO to address in their first 18 months:

Operational Infrastructure - Complete the modernization of internal systems, documentation, and workflows to match the organization's external reputation
CRM & Data Management - Lead or oversee resolution of the EveryAction database challenges; manual workarounds are not sustainable. Consider forming a technology task force.
Fundraising Diversification - Move beyond reliance on a small number of donors and grants; build an annual giving program and cultivate a broader individual donor base
Governing Board Transition - Complete the shift from working board to governing board, with clearly defined roles, responsibilities, and committee structure between board, CEO, and staff
Statewide Expansion - Deepen reach beyond the Indianapolis metro through local ambassador models, listening sessions, and coalition partnerships
C3/C4 Clarity - Establish clear structures and resource allocation between the two entities, particularly as staff time is split across both

What You'll Bring

Leadership experience in nonprofit, public, or private sector organizations
Demonstrated success in strategic planning, organizational sustainability, and operational leadership
Proven fundraising experience, including major gifts and institutional funding
Strong financial acumen, including budgeting and resource allocation
Experience working with or supporting governing boards
Ability to build partnerships across community, business, and government sectors

Wipfli is assisting our client, Kewa Pueblo Health Corporation (KPHC), in seeking an experienced and mission-driven Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead the organization. This is a unique opportunity for an accomplished healthcare executive to guide a tribally chartered healthcare organization, strengthen programs and services, and help ensure the highest quality of care for the Santo Domingo Pueblo community.

Located between Albuquerque and Santa Fe on the Santo Domingo (Kewa) Pueblo, KPHC is a community-based health center operating under an Indian Health Service (IHS) Title I contract. Dedicated to ensuring health and wellness through excellence in healthcare with respect for culture, KPHC has grown from a primary care clinic into a comprehensive, multidisciplinary health system offering primary care, dental, optometry, pharmacy, behavioral health, public health, and specialty services, helping community members and patients access high-quality care close to home.

Reporting directly to the KPHC Board of Directors, the CEO is responsible for the overall administration and programmatic oversight of all KPHC programs and services, including the Santo Domingo Health Center. The CEO exercises executive authority for operational decisions, works closely with the Board on the management and direction of the Health Center, and provides leadership across operations, quality, compliance, finance, workforce development, strategic planning, and community relationships.

Key Responsibilities

Executive Leadership and Organizational Direction

Provide overall leadership and direction for KPHC programs, services, facilities, and health services provided to the community.
Work closely with the KPHC Board of Directors to manage and direct the Corporation’s programs and services.
Set and advance the mission, vision, and values of KPHC programs and services.
Lead long-range program planning and development of a strategic plan that addresses the health needs of the Santo Domingo Pueblo.
Make operational decisions, recommend new or revised policies, and ensure consistent implementation of approved policies and procedures.
Maintain ongoing, effective communication throughout the Corporation.

Operations, Quality, and Regulatory Compliance

Plan, organize, and direct facility operations to support quality care and the financial integrity of KPHC.
Coordinate quality assurance, quality improvement, and regulatory compliance across services offered to the community.
Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, Board policies, medical staff requirements, AAAHC standards, and other regulatory agencies.
Oversee systems for patient grievances, external appeals, adverse or sentinel event reporting, privacy, fraud and abuse prevention, and NPDB reporting.
Ensure appropriate maintenance and improvements for all KPHC facilities, grounds, and infrastructure.

Financial Stewardship and Resource Development

Collaborate with the Chief Financial Officer to monitor accounting, budgeting, responsibility reporting, internal controls, auditing, and cost reporting systems.
Oversee financial reporting, budget preparation and maintenance, billing, payroll, and related fiscal policies.
Prepare and administer the annual budget in coordination with the Finance Department and advise executive staff and the Board regarding shortages or needed adjustments.
Pursue alternate resources to support program activity, including grants, contracts, staffing agreements, and third-party reimbursements.
Oversee the Corporation’s performance of programs, functions, services, and activities assumed from the Indian Health Service under Public Law 93-638 or other funding source

Workforce Leadership and Development

Supervise the executive staff, complete performance evaluations, provide job training and orientation, and evaluate and implement performance management systems specific to departmental needs, including assignment of duties, work schedules, leave requests, and monitoring of work standards.
Coordinate staff development and ensure compliance with continuing education requirements for all KPHC employees.
Hold staff accountable for performance and performance improvement, and recognize, motivate, and reward positive results.
Adhere to non-discriminatory employment practices and, in conjunction with Human Resources, develop an affirmative action plan with appropriate objectives and goals and communicate those to employees.

Board, Tribal, and Community Relations

Attend monthly KPHC Board meetings and provide reports on program workload, staffing, accomplishments, challenges, healthcare trends, and other matters affecting governance oversight.
Act as a liaison among KPHC programs, Santo Domingo tribal programs, Indian Health Service, the State of New Mexico, and other outside agencies.
Represent KPHC and the Pueblo of Santo Domingo on health-related boards and committees, as appropriate.
Encourage integration of the medical facility and services with the community through communication, visibility, and public outreach.
Maintain effective communication throughout the Corporation and with the Board, staff, community, and external partners.
Perform other related administrative and leadership duties as necessary or in the best interest of KPHC and/or as requested by the Board.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Master’s degree in public health administration, health administration, business administration, public administration, or another related health or business field required.
Five or more (5+) years of progressive management, administration, and supervisory experience in an executive capacity within the healthcare field required.
Experience with human resources management and the development and administration of financial management processes and systems required.
Knowledge of rural, community-oriented healthcare delivery systems and associated regulations and standards.
Knowledge and experience with Public Law 93-638 Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act contracting and the Indian Health Service system.
Knowledge of personnel management, fund accounting, finance, business administration, budget development and control, accreditation, certification, privacy, and healthcare compliance requirements.
Demonstrated experience in strategic planning, problem analysis, consequence projection, solution identification, and implementation of recommendations.
Ability to lead, train, supervise, and evaluate professional and paraprofessional healthcare providers and to build effective relationships across varying social and cultural backgrounds.
Excellent English-language verbal and written communication skills and proficiency with business technology, including Word, Excel, Access, and presentation software.
Ability to maintain confidentiality, exercise sound judgment, manage multiple priorities and deadlines, and uphold professional and ethical standards.
Commitment to integrity, cultural humility, and stewardship of organizational resources.
Preferred: Ten or more (10+) years of executive-level management experience in healthcare; prior experience working with Indian Health Service, a Tribe, or a Tribal organization; bilingual skills in English and the Keres native language.

About the Community

This position is based on-site at the Santo Domingo Health Center in New Mexico, nestled in the heart of the Kewa Pueblo between the vibrant cultural hubs of Albuquerque and Santa Fe. The region offers an exceptional quality of life, combining rich cultural heritage, stunning high-desert landscapes, and a deep sense of community. Residents enjoy year-round sunshine, world-renowned arts and cuisine, outdoor recreation, and easy access to two of the Southwest's most dynamic cities, each less than an hour away. For a health care executive seeking the opportunity to drive meaningful change while practicing medicine in a truly unique, mission-driven setting, KPHC offers the best of both career and community.

Employee Benefits

At KPHC, we invest in our employees by offering a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, financial well-being, work-life balance, and professional growth. Eligible employees may enjoy:
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance options for employees and eligible dependents.
Retirement savings plan with employer contributions.
Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) program.
Relocation assistance to support your transition.
Life and disability insurance coverage.
Continuing education and professional development support.

If you are a collaborative, community-minded executive who is energized by the opportunity to strengthen tribal healthcare and make a meaningful impact in the community we serve, we encourage you to submit your resume through our application portal to be considered for this exciting opportunity.

of Grants Management
based in Washington, D.C. The Managing Director of Grants Management is eligible for a hybrid work schedule, including Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday required on-site in the Washington, D.C. office.

Skoll is a private grantmaking foundation that seeks to build a sustainable world of peace and prosperity for all by investing in, connecting, and championing social entrepreneurs and other social innovators. Together, we advance bold and equitable solutions to the world’s most pressing problems. The Skoll Foundation fosters a mission and values-based approach to the work we do focused on the vision of doing good.

Position Description

Reporting directly to the General Counsel, the Managing Director of Grants Management leads the Foundation’s grants management team in the execution and fulfillment of Foundation grants designed by our program teams. This role leads the short- and long-term strategy for grants management, including supporting the administration of approximately $100 million in grants each year. The Managing Director will be an internal expert on private foundation grantmaking, will provide support and training on grantmaking practices within the Foundation, and will build strong working relationships across programs to execute grantmaking strategies and advance the Foundation’s mission. The Managing Director serves as a trusted advisor and key partner to a wide range of internal and external stakeholders and directs a centralized approach to grantmaking systems, compliance, policies, and processes that are optimized for the Foundation’s innovative grantmaking environment. The Managing Director will also oversee external grants management vendor relationships and partners (Silicon Valley Community Foundation, Submittable, etc.) in the execution of the Foundation’s grantmaking activities and will consider ways to continually advance the efficiency and effectiveness of the Foundation’s grantmaking operations. The Managing Director will have one direct report, the Grants Manager. With a team of this size, both roles are expected to work directly on the grants pipeline: the Managing Director will regularly review and process grants alongside the Grants Manager, in addition to leading the function's strategy and standards. 

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

Strategy and Leadership

Provide leadership on the design and day-to-day operations of grants management, with a keen eye for efficiency and service quality. Build and maintain feedback mechanisms to ensure early detection of end-user problems. Apply foresight and judgment in adjusting grants management service, training, and communications to support program goals. 

Design and manage the overall grant workflow to support the full grant lifecycle, including pipeline management, grant recommendation, board approval process, grant agreement execution, payments, amendments, and reporting. Identify opportunities to streamline and improve the grantmaking workflow, further partner with external vendors, and enhance user training on systems and processes.

Partner with Finance on short- and long-term grants budget planning, including the development of the annual grant allocation and payout. Regularly advise teams on progress toward the current fiscal year’s grant payout while also ensuring flexibility in future years. 

Support the development of the Grants Manager, overseeing training, professional development, and performance management. 

Grants Management

Oversee all aspects of pre-and post-award grant activities, including supporting the full lifecycle of the grant process, from review, approval, payment, reporting, amendments, and closeout.

Review all grants, programmatic contracts, and Program-Related Investments for compliance with IRS regulations and Foundation requirements, working in partnership with the Grants Manager and collaborating with legal to ensure resolution of complex grantmaking issues, as needed.

Regularly participate in program meetings to advise and guide teams on appropriate charitable giving mechanisms to achieve programmatic objectives and impact, necessary legal due diligence, and to collaborate on pipeline planning.

Serve as primary relationship manager for the Foundation’s grantmaking partner, Silicon Valley Community Foundation, in the administration of the Skoll Fund, including coordinating fund grant recommendations, reconciling grants management system data against provider records, monitoring compliance with fund requirements, and partnering with Finance and Legal on entity selection for grant awards.

Develop institutional grantmaking policies and procedures for staff and grantees. This includes overseeing the development and maintenance of a grants management manual that joins the Foundation’s grantmaking policies, processes, and tools with complete grantmaking system documentation.

In close partnership with the Finance Department, oversee development of the annual grants-related data for Skoll Foundation’s 990-PF and Skoll Fund’s 990. Support Finance staff with the annual audit requirements.

Systems, Data, and Reporting

Partner with the Technology Team on infrastructure, security, integration standards, and architecture review.

Advise, coordinate, and collaborate on Foundation data strategy and governance for grantmaking data, including determining what data to capture and report for internal and external audiences.

In collaboration with internal teams, continually review, refine, and re-align on definitions and consistent uses of programmatic codes and tags, and regularly review grantmaking data to ensure accurate representation of information for data analysis purposes.

Prepare reports and data visualizations to provide a clear and compelling illustration of the Foundation’s grantmaking for internal and external stakeholders.

Design, monitor, and report on key operational metrics for the grantmaking function, e.g., annual trends on grant types and transaction volume, to support continuous improvement and inform resourcing decisions.

Continually stay abreast of new developments in Foundation grants management systems and technologies and their applicability to the evolving needs of the Foundation.  

Sector Engagement

Research, synthesize, and share knowledge on grantmaking practices and funding mechanisms that are relevant to the Foundation.

Advocate for equitable, values-aligned grantmaking approaches consistent with the Foundation’s mission.
